note: The quest content this world pack carries (crates/asura-world/src/quest.rs, docs/58-quests.md). Every unit is the live capture's: the client resolves encoded units through its own string table, and this server never composes or resolves them. A quest's marker is the capture's exact bits; both +infinity means the capture showed no marker.

fields.quests: One per quest id the catalog or the capture names.
fields.id: The client's quest id: the number a log entry, a marker and a request carry.
fields.state: The captured log state: bit 1 loaded, bit 2 completed, bit 32 primary. The server masks bits 1 and 2 when it restores an entry.
fields.marker: The log marker: x_bits and y_bits are exact IEEE-754 bit patterns, and plane is the map plane. Both +infinity means no marker.
fields.map_to: The map the marker points at. 898 is the no-destination sentinel these captures carry.
fields.map_from: The map the quest was taken on.
fields.location: The quest log's category, encoded units.
fields.name: The quest's name, encoded units; at most 7 units plus the client's own terminator.
fields.npc: The quest giver's name, encoded units; at most 7 units plus the terminator.
fields.description: The 0x004C details text, encoded units; at most 127 units plus the terminator.
fields.objectives: The 0x004C objectives text, encoded units; at most 127 units plus the terminator.
fields.character_argument: The captured character name inside the text. The server replaces it with the playing character's name, between 0x0107 and 0x0001.
fields.completed: The details the capture shows after the quest completed.
fields.counted: The details the capture shows after this many objective credits, contiguous from 1.
fields.credits: How many objective credits this variant was captured at.
fields.offer: Who offers the quest, on which map, and to whom: requires_none_completed, requires_rewarded, requires_any_rewarded, professions (primary_only), min_level; and the skills accepting teaches. Written by tools/npc-content-from-captures.py.
fields.reward: Who takes the turn-in, on which map, and what it pays: experience, gold and skill_points (the quest's own reward text), the skills it teaches, and requires_completed when the turn-in waits for a modelled objective.
